headline: Debora now needs moderate help with bathing and lower-body dressing, and a documented Oct 2 fall conflicts with later notes saying it was charted on the wrong participant.

items.statement: The RN documented a fall at home on 2026-10-02 in the kitchen. Kevin found her on the floor. She had a small left forearm skin tear and denied head strike or loss of consciousness. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed. Notes dated 2026-10-06 and 2026-10-09 say this entry was charted on the wrong participant. That conflict is unresolved (see questions).
items.verifier_note: The statement reports the fall as documented, with every detail matching the 10-02 RN note. It also notes that the 10-06 and 10-09 notes dispute it and leaves the conflict unresolved for the team.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 the OT found Debora needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing. She was independent at the last review. The OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower, and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: All details match the OT note of 10-26.

items.statement: On 2026-10-19 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting Debora out of the tub. Debora said she has been skipping showers because she is afraid of slipping.
items.verifier_note: The home care aide note of 10-19 matches the statement.

items.statement: The PT evaluation on 2026-10-05 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommends a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, and bathroom grab bars. PT will see her twice weekly. The evaluation references the disputed Oct 2 fall.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation details match note n006. The statement also flags the Oct 2 fall as disputed, which is backed by the correction notes.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, her spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. Respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: The social work note of 10-13 matches the statement.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14). The pharmacist reconciled it on 2026-09-15. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks. No recheck or repeat PHQ-9 appears in the notes provided.
items.verifier_note: The start date, dose, PHQ-9, pharmacist reconciliation and 4-week recheck plan all match the sources. The cited notes contain no recheck or repeat PHQ-9.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded this season (season start 2026-08-01). The last dose was on 2026-04-25.
items.verifier_note: The immunization record shows flu_vaccine_this_season is false for the season starting 2026-08-01. The last dose was 2026-04-25.

questions_for_team: Was the 2026-10-02 fall charted on the wrong participant? The RN and PT notes document it, while the HIM and social work notes call it an error. Who will verify this, and how should the PT referral and fall-risk rating be handled in the meantime?

Whatever the answer on the Oct 2 fall, her tub-transfer help, fear of slipping, and Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds are documented separately. How will bathing safety and equipment (transfer bench, handheld shower, walker, grab bars) be addressed?
Should home care hours increase for bathing support, as the OT recommends?
Has the 4-week sertraline recheck and repeat PHQ-9 been done, and who owns it?
What respite and evening support can be arranged for Kevin, and who will follow up?

mammogram oncology surveillance breast cancer follow-up
pain score cognition memory confusion cognitive screen
lab results HbA1c TSH lipid LDL liver panel bleeding bruising

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, urgent care visits, and hospital admissions in that window, plus any since the last IDT review, with reasons and discharge summaries.

Falls and near-falls: count and document any falls, injuries, or fall-risk screen changes in the window; note whether she is on new sedating or antidepressant medication, since sertraline was started 2026-09-13 within the window.

Sertraline start (2026-09-13) for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14): confirm prescriber, dose, and indication; check for a follow-up PHQ-9 or mood reassessment date, adverse effects (GI upset, sleep change, dizziness, hyponatremia signs), and whether bleeding risk is discussed given concurrent clopidogrel.
Depression and mood overall: review PHQ-9 trend, any suicidality screen, social withdrawal, and attendance at PACE day programming during the window.

Cardiac status (ischemic heart disease, onset 2025): review chest pain or nitroglycerin spray use, heart rate and blood pressure trend on metoprolol succinate, and any cardiology follow-up in the window.
Antiplatelet and statin review: confirm clopidogrel and simvastatin are still active and adherent, check for any bleeding or bruising events, and verify lipid/liver monitoring is current if due.

Respiratory status (COPD/chronic obstructive bronchitis, chronic sinusitis): review albuterol and fluticasone/salmeterol use frequency, oxygen saturation readings, exacerbations, steroid courses, and inhaler technique or refill gaps (inhalers started 2026-04-25).
Breast cancer history (malignant neoplasm, 2000): check oncology surveillance status, any new symptoms, and whether survivorship follow-up or imaging is due in the window.
Thyroid (idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 0.075 mg): check whether TSH monitoring is due or resulted, and any missed doses.
Metabolic and weight: review weight trend (BMI 30+ history), prediabetes labs (HbA1c or glucose) if due, and dietary or activity counseling status.
Chronic pain: review pain scores, analgesic use (none listed as active, so confirm any OTC or PRN use not captured), and pain impact on ADLs and sleep.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: compare current ADL and IADL scores against the last review, note any decline, and check mobility aids and home safety.
Cognition: review any cognitive screen results or staff observations of memory or confusion, especially with new medication and mood change.
Caregiver and social situation: confirm caregiver availability, any change in living situation or transportation (she is in Los Angeles), and caregiver strain.
Care-plan items due: list goals, assessments, and reviews with due dates falling in or before 2026-11-30, and flag any overdue items for the IDT agenda.
Allergy record: allergies field is empty; confirm allergy status with the patient and pharmacy and reconcile before the meeting.
Summarize changes for the IDT as items for discussion only (new sertraline start, any ED or admission, falls, weight or BP shifts, function changes), without making treatment recommendations.
